subject: Whether a live control can be named from Logic's own data, without position and without a translated label
question: AX exposes localised strings. Is there a canonical Logic asset that a live AX reading can be reversed into, yielding the same identifier in every locale?

reverify.expected: 62 tests pass, including test_the_live_axhelp_corpus_is_explained_by_canonical_data, which asserts over the 114 distinct AXHelp values in docs/observations/evidence/2026-09-15-axhelp-live-values.txt and requires exactly one unresolved. That case needs Logic installed; it reads the bundle and launches nothing.
reverify.cost: ~2s; reads the app bundle, launches nothing

method: Composed each QuickHelp entry as "{Title}. {Text}" in all ten locales, then tried to reverse the 114 distinct AXHelp values of a live ko-KR dump back into QuickHelp keys. Separately checked whether the nib runtime attribute qhid reaches the same keys. The dump truncates long values, so exact matching was supplemented with prefix and containment matching, counted separately.

observations.what: live AXHelp reversed into QuickHelp keys
the composition rule, measured rather than guessed
prefix_carries: its own title and key equivalent
live object state (a region's bar range)
the reason the control is disabled
examples: KCE_024_Record -> '녹음   R, 녹음 버튼. 선택한 트랙 또는 녹음 준비된 여러 트랙에 녹음합니다.'
ARR_021_MidiRegion -> '리전은 1 마디 에서 시작하여 2 마디 에서 끝납니다., MIDI 리전. MIDI 노트 및 …'
TRA_073_TunerButton -> '이 컨트롤을 사용할 수 없습니다. 원인: 오디오 트랙이 선택되지 않았습니다., 튜너 버튼. …'

observations.what: nib qhid, which I had proposed as the handle

observations.audio_plug_in: '오디오 플러그인' is AXDescription, not AXHelp, and comes from MAMixer.framework Localizable.strings. Different attribute, so it does not bear on the AXHelp rule.
observations.region_sentence: '리전은 N 마디 에서 시작하여 …' does come from a Logic.framework template, and it is AXHelp. It is the runtime PREFIX; the same value's suffix is QuickHelp ARR_021_MidiRegion. Both sources are in one string.

observations.what: the second layer, where QuickHelp does not explain the value at all
observations.note: These are Logic.framework's own string tables. The shortcut tier is the table's value plus a run of spaces and a key equivalent added at runtime; the template tier is one canonical format string rendering several live values.

conclusion: AXHelp is QuickHelp.plist with a runtime prefix. On 86 of 114 distinct live values the QuickHelp composition "{Title}. {Text}" appears, and in 86 of 86 it sits at the END of the value with no exception; 56 values are the QuickHelp composition alone and 30 carry a prefix ending in a comma. The prefix is live data -- the control's current value, its key equivalent, a region's bar range, or the reason it is disabled -- so one AXHelp reading yields both a canonical identifier and the control's state. Because QuickHelp ships in ten locales with identical 9835-key keysets, that identifier is the same in every locale, and for 9502 keys the set of keys sharing a string is identical in all ten, 5982 of them one to one. This is a locale-independent control handle taken from Logic's own data rather than from position or a translated label. It is NOT the handle I proposed earlier: nib qhid reaches QuickHelp keys (587 of 619) but only 1 of the 86 live-matched controls carried one, so qhid links static nib assets, not the surfaces this repository drives. Every matched key was symbolic; none of the 4061 numeric keys was reached.
limits: One dump, one locale (ko-KR), one set of open windows. 114 distinct AXHelp values is a small slice of the application, and no claim is made about what fraction of all controls expose AXHelp at all.

The suffix rule is what makes the containment tier trustworthy, and it was checked only on these 86. A QuickHelp string short enough to occur by accident inside an unrelated AXHelp would still match; the shortest fragment relied on here is 26 characters.
The dump truncates values at 163 characters. Values longer than that were matched on their visible part.
This establishes AXHelp -> key. It does not establish key -> control: nothing here shows a wanted key can be used to FIND a control on screen, only that a control already in hand can be named.
The 28 unmatched values were not explained. Several are short mixer view toggles ('Aux 채널 스트립 표시', '넓은 채널 스트립') that are likely drawn from a framework Localizable.strings the way '오디오 플러그인' is.
Locale invariance was computed from the shipped plists, not observed live. Whether Logic running in de-DE emits the de-DE composition was not measured.

The prefix grammar is described from 30 examples. Whether the separator is always a comma, and whether a prefix can itself contain the separator, was not established -- a parser must therefore anchor on the QuickHelp suffix, not split on the comma.

the second resolver layer: this value plus a run of spaces and a key equivalent is the whole of a live AXHelp that QuickHelp cannot explain. Bound to this record rather than to Scripts/logic_canon.py: the value appears there only inside a comment, and the comment-stripping added after review correctly refused it

the template layer: one canonical template renders eight of the live AXHelp values, with the channel-strip type as its argument. Bound to this record rather than to Scripts/logic_canon.py: the value appears there only inside a comment, and the comment-stripping added after review correctly refused it

canon_absent.claim: one live AXHelp value has no canonical source anywhere in the Logic bundle
canon_absent.why_runtime: An exhaustive scan of all 75,535 non-media files in the bundle, in UTF-8 and both UTF-16 byte orders, found it nowhere, and a separate scan of all 1,169 nibs found it nowhere. It is most plausibly drawn from AppKit, whose localised strings live in the dyld shared cache rather than in files this corpus can hold -- and that plausibility is stated as unverified: the shared cache was not opened.
